_comment: Real IBANforge API responses, replayed by the README-execution test of BOTH SDKs.
This file is DATA, never hand-edited: run `node sdks/fixtures/record.mjs <base-url>`.
`--check` re-plays every request and fails on any difference — that is the pre-publish gate.
Every call listed here is one a README block actually makes. Adding a call to a README
without adding it here makes the stub answer 599 and the test fail, on purpose.
Recorded against a server in IBANFORGE_FREE_MODE=true, so `cost_usdc` reads 0 here; production charges the price listed in the README table. No README asserts on it.
`used_by` says which README(s) exercise the call. Each SDK's test asserts both directions: nothing it uses is unlisted, nothing listed for it goes unused.

calls.name: keys-generate
calls.why: the one-line free key. The address must survive our own disposable-domain guard. Recorded FIRST: the key it returns authenticates every call below, so recording needs no key handed in. `--check` skips it — a second creation from the same network is legitimately guarded (403/429), not drift.

meta.disclaimer: Informational triage only — NOT a regulated AML/CFT product. Sanctions screening is performed at the BANK (BIC8) level: it flags the holding institution, NOT the beneficiary / account-holder name. Most sanctions designations target persons and companies, which this does not screen. Use a regulated provider (Refinitiv, ComplyAdvantage, etc.) for name-level KYC/AML obligations.
meta.country_risk_scope: risk_indicators.country_risk is a separate editorial AML axis (offshore centres, conflict zones, EBA-flagged jurisdictions) layered ON TOP of compliance.sanctions.fatf_status, not a restatement of it. The two can disagree on a country by design; each carries its own review date.
